newsitem.title: UK: LME copper volatility may increase again - Merrill.
newsitem.headline: LME copper volatility may increase again - Merrill.

text.p: Copper price volatility could increase again on the London Metal Exchange (LME), with the fundamental market close to balance, according to U.S. brokerage Merill Lynch.
"...as the copper market is currently about in balance to being in a small surplus there is considerable scope for prices to become more volatile," Merrill said in a monthly report.
The scope for greater volatility would increase if a U.S. bank understood to be holding some of Sumitomo Corp's old positions decided to try to run values higher, Merill added.

"This volatility...would be greatly enhanced if the big U.S. investment bank that is widely reported to have taken over Sumitomo's positions on its own account decided to do a bit of squeezing itself," the report said.
Merrill said the bank could try to push prices up to $2,000 a tonne ahead of options declarations "over coming months" to trigger covering from option grantors short of the strike.
By removing stocks from LME warehouses, the bank "and some of its close associates" could "force prices higher almost at will," the report said.
The bank and its associates "are...thought to control a large chunk of the existing LME copper stocks."
"So it is an easy matter to tighten the market in the short term if this bank and its associates want to," Merrill said.
Merrill added that Sumitomo was not the only firm in the past to try to squeeze the copper market.
"A great number of merchant firms were (and still are) active in this activity," the Merrill report said.
